source_contract.second_class_scope_rule: Accepted Chapter 6 propositions are outside subsections explicitly marked [一等].

review_basis: current official MLIT 第5版 source/locators

decisions.rationale: 6.1 supports takeoff/landing-site checks for structures that may cause compass error; distinct from Q091 multi-constraint integration.
6.1 supports high-voltage-facility and aircraft-traffic checks; distinct from Q091 because this tests hazard identification and route choice.
6.1 supports planning for foreseeable changes; no released item tests this checklist boundary directly.
6.1 supports checking planned route/time for temporary restrictions; Q091 gives such a constraint as already established.
6.1 explicitly addresses visual-limit distance ambiguity, onsite confirmation, and assistant placement; distinct from Q092 generic obstacle avoidance.
Same answer-defining proposition as Q045: low temperature can shorten battery endurance/flight time; reserve-margin scenario does not add a distinct reasoning target.
6.2 supports heated-surface/solar-panel local updraft risk; no released item tests this proposition.
6.2 supports strong-sunlight broad-ground updraft/dust-devil risk; distinct from released general wind/gust items.
6.2 says thunder is a postpone/cancel condition. Q096 tests fog; this adds the distinct pre-rain thunder decision boundary and misconception.
6.2 supports daytime sea breeze toward warmer land and nighttime land breeze toward sea; no released item tests this reversal.
6.2 supports daytime valley wind/nighttime mountain wind; distinct terrain/time reasoning.
Q035 already tests the same building-wind proposition: nearby open-site wind cannot be directly applied to a high-rise site because building arrangement creates local wind.
6.2 supports short-lived local downburst/microburst events that may escape ordinary observation networks; distinct from Q094/Q036.
6.3 supports headwind takeoff/landing and tailwind stall risk; Q097 tests spatial constraints instead.
6.3 states fixed-wing aircraft cannot hover and use circling for loiter; distinct from Q097's broader area/turn-radius proposition.
6.3 supports helicopter ground-effect risk near/below approximately main-rotor radius; Q098 tests takeoff-area separation, not ground effect.
6.3 supports strong downslope wind limiting helicopter climb; distinct aircraft-specific performance decision.
6.3 supports VRS risk in vertical/low-speed descent and forward-descent mitigation; no released item tests this hazard.
6.3 states autorotation has required operations and valid height/speed ranges; distinct from Q044 emergency landing-site planning.
6.4 supports night visual human-factor risk. Q100 gives that risk as a premise and tests lighting controls; C020 tests risk recognition itself.
6.4 requires prior night training in a safe no-third-party place; distinct from Q100 lighting controls.
6.4 supports the broader BVLOS capability set. Q038 isolates position+abnormality; C022 tests completeness across autopilot/camera/state awareness/failsafe.
6.4 gives radio-loss failsafe examples of automatic return or position hold; no released item tests this contingency.
6.4 no-assistant BVLOS supports conspicuity by lights/recognizable paint; purpose is distinct from Q100 operator night visibility.
6.4 no-assistant BVLOS requires broad ground state/weather/route-deviation monitoring; distinct from Q038 assistant-present position/abnormality scope.
